Signs of the World

Phone

History

The 1949 Geneva Protocol on Road Signs and Signals marked telephones with a handset and its cord on a white square. The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends a similar symbol design. In the 1970s, US designers found the shape common but easy to mistake for a wrench.

Adoption

The handset now means "call" on phones around the world, outliving the shape of the telephones it came from. The ISO 7010 safety standard uses it for emergency phones.
